route_status.proven_scope: The focused scripted probe instantiates the bathroom cleanup owner, confirms the dirty interactive room and basket invitation, triggers its internal basket-tap seam, and checks handoff into sink cleaning. Source review confirms production synchronization is conditional on an active Day One bubble_bath room.
route_status.gaps: The probe does not enter the bathroom through the ordinary fresh-save child route or exercise the visible Button with routed screen-touch input. It calls setup(main, false), disabling spoken announcements; voice checks include static source wiring and a prompt-state flag. It supplies no rendered phone view, device latency check, child observation, or owner review.

source_constants.value: Initial spoken hint is deferred after setup; code text is ‘Tap the cleaning basket.’

timing.assumptions: No child session duration is inferred. Probe runner wall time is not gameplay timing.

tactile.target_size: A 220×220 base-canvas Button overlays the basket at scripts/games/day_one_bathroom_cleanup.gd:724-734; source defines the physical basket at (940,575), scale 0.105 (lines 72-74). Probe and 110×110 guidance support a generous target by dimensions only; no device projection or touch feel was measured.
tactile.press_response: Code connects Button.pressed to _on_basket_tapped; the handler sets busy, plays UI tap and contextual voice when announcements are enabled, then marks both supplies found and starts the cleaning handoff (lines 734,789-806). The probe invoked probe_tap_basket() directly rather than the visible button.
tactile.drag_hold_release: Not part of this first action; code comment states the basket is the single tap action and no magnifier/drag surface is playable (lines 6-8,355-367).
tactile.ownership: The button is a transparent physical-object hit region on the visible basket and world controls are suppressed while this overlay owns the rescue (lines 724-734; 647-662). One-finger device ownership was not evaluated here.
tactile.cancellation: This review did not exercise cancellation of the initial basket tap; focused probe covers teardown/restoration, but not an actual routed press cancellation.

play_appeal.hypothesis: One focused tap followed by the sponge visibly traveling toward the sink may make the first cause and effect legible. The basket pulse, moving hand pointer, spoken hint, and prompt repeaters offer multiple cues without a reading task. Whether this feels inviting or obvious at phone size needs visual and child evidence.

The handler’s first tap reveals both tools and hands off to a visible sponge-to-sink demonstration; the probe reports no assertion failures.
